title.narrative: Enhancing Transparency and Accountability in Domestic Debt Management in Kenya

description.narrative: Kenya's public debt landscape has undergone significant shifts in recent years, with a growing reliance on domestic borrowing as outlined in the Medium-Term Debt Management Strategy (MTDS). As of May 2025, domestic debt accounted for over 56% of total public debt, largely comprised of short-term, high-interest Treasury bills and bonds. While this trend reflects a deliberate policy pivot to reduce external vulnerabilities, it has also brought to the fore several gaps in the governance, transparency, and accountability of domestic debt management. The core issue this project seeks to address is the institutional and civic invisibility of domestic debt governance. Unlike external debt, where parliamentary oversight, audit reviews, and civil society engagement have seen notable growth, domestic debt remains relatively less scrutinized. Parliament has historically focused its energy on external loans, donor-funded projects, and multilateral agreements, often overlooking the terms, risks, and equity implications of domestic borrowing. Similarly, public participation in debt discourse is minimal, partly due to the technical complexity of instruments and a lack of accessible, timely information
